what_it_does: BQSim accelerates quantum circuit simulation on GPUs. Quantum simulators typically process one input state (initial quantum state) at a time, but verification and testing need to run the same circuit on thousands of slightly different inputs. BQSim recognizes that many of these computations are identical: if two input states are similar, the circuit operations overlap significantly. It uses decision diagrams (a compact representation of computation trees that identifies duplicate sub-expressions) to find this shared structure, then converts these diagrams into GPU-optimized data structures. A scheduling system groups related computations into batches before sending them to the GPU, reducing kernel launch overhead. The decision diagram optimization collapses redundant operations, so the GPU does less total work for all inputs combined.
